Shchyrets Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Shchyrets's Jewish community, first documented in 1629, was subordinated to the kehila of Komarno, documented elsewhere in this collection, in the early 18th century. In the late 19th century, the head of the town's Jewish community also served as its mayor — a notable instance of a Jewish communal leader simultaneously holding the town's top civic office. The population reached an extraordinary 78.9 percent of the town by 1880. In August and November 1942, more than 1,000 Jews were deported to the Bibrka ghetto — the same destination documented at Novi Strilyshcha elsewhere in this collection — and to the Bełżec death camp.
